title: atomic undo plan and hypotheses
body:
Quick context:
- Working on a medium-risk refactor that changes how incremental KV cache writes are gated during warmup. Goal was lower tail latency variance for short sequences but it touches the hotpath.
- PR is fairly small (3 files, ~220 LOC), but touches cache sync + replica sync logic -> risk of state divergence.

Objectives for this scratchpad:
1) Define a small, reliable "atomic undo" plan that can be executed post-merge with minimal disruption.
2) List hypotheses and quick experiments to validate rollback assumptions.
3) Draft a minimal checklist for on-call / SRE to use if we see anomalies.

Topline undo strategy (high-level):
- If divergence or correctness regressions observed: do a targeted revert of the PR and follow a defined data-compatibility sequence. Avoid broad infra restarts.
- Prefer fast, low-blast radius mitigations first: pin to previous model variant, disable warmup path via runtime flag, then revert code if needed.

Step-by-step rollback playbook (fast path):
1) Detect: anomaly triggers (see "Signals to watch").
2) Mitigate: flip runtime feature flag `kv_warmup_optim` = false (no deploy, feature flag immediate).
3) If mitigated -> schedule follow-up revert + postmortem.
4) If not mitigated -> revert PR with emergency revert PR and run canary (see steps below).
5) If revert PR negative impact -> revert revert and escalate to offline rollback with SRE.

Commands (ops quick-cookbook):
- Create emergency revert branch: git checkout -b revert/pr-2841 && git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha> && gh pr create --title "emergency: revert pr-2841" --body "auto revert, follow up in ticket ENG-7891"
- Push & assign SRE reviewer + set label "rollback-emergency"

Signals to watch (immediate, top-of-runbook):
- Error spike: 5xx rate > baseline +3% sustained over 5m for the route.
- Divergence: KV checksum mismatch reports from the replica-sync job (important).
- Latency tail: p99 increase > 30% compared to rolling baseline for short-seq routes.
- Customer-facing errors: any increase in user-visible incorrect outputs flagged by QA.

Canary matrix (post-revert or post-flag flip):
- Canary cohort: 2% traffic to canary cluster with new flag off, 10k requests min sample. Run for 30m.
- Metrics: 5xx rate, p95/p99 tokens, KV checksum success ratio, droppped prefix hits.
- Success criteria: 5xx rate within 0.5x of baseline delta; checksum mismatches <= 0; latency tail within 10% of baseline.

Hypotheses (to test quickly):
H1: The warmup write gating reduces tail latency but occasionally races with replica sync, causing checksum mismatches.
- Quick test: locally instrument replica-sync to log timestamps and emit synthetic mismatch injection. Run with 1000 short-seq requests.
H2: Turning off warmup gating removes mismatches but increases p95 by ~5-8% on short sequences.
- Quick test: A/B with feature flag enabled/disabled using loadgen.
H3: State divergence only occurs under high-burst scenarios when batch size > 12 and sequence length < 32.
- Quick test: synthetic bursts with varying batch sizes.

Experiment checklist (minimal):
- Create a sandbox cluster with single-replica to repro faster.
- Add lightweight tracing: record (request_id, cache_write_ts, replica_apply_ts, checksum_pre, checksum_post).
- Run replay of recorded production traces focusing on short-seq tails.
- Document an example trace that reproduces mismatch (attach as artifact to ENG-7891).

Testing matrix (unit/integration):
- Unit: validate cache write atomicity with mocked replica client (new tests: 3 cases: normal, delayed replica ack, partial failure).
- Integration: small-scale cluster test with simulated network jitter.
- End-to-end: run 10k requests from loadgen with golden expected outputs and checksum diffing.

Post-merge follow-ups (owner rotation):
- Day 0: owner (me) watches for the first 6 hours; be reachable via pager; slack channel #kv-cache-rollout.
- Day 1: hand off to Ravi for extended monitoring & metrics dashboard refinement.
- Day 3: if stable, add automated regression alert (p99 delta > X%) and remove pager.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Can we make the checksum alert more actionable? Right now it fires as a metric but lacks context (which shard, which request). Need to attach request_id traces.
- Is the feature flag low-latency enough? It's fast in staging but will it propagate in-host quickly enough for live mitigation? Test propagation on a few clusters.
- Edge-case: what happens if revert occurs while there are partially-applied writes? Need list of clean-up steps to resync replicas. Possibly a one-shot resync job that should be safe — confirm list of idempotent ops.
- Communications: draft short status template for customers if we must escalate.

Draft status/notes to self:
- This is intentionally conservative: prefer quick flag-off over immediate revert where possible.
- Keep the emergency revert PR atomic and minimal; avoid mixing other changes.
- After any rollback, capture a minimal repro and attach to ENG-7891 before unassigning the owner.

Next immediate actions (today):
- Add basic tracing logs in a non-blocking way and re-run local replay (ETA 2h).
- Add the feature-flag flip runbook entry to the runbook doc (linked artifact).
- Ask SRE (Mina) to sanity-check the canary thresholds.

Related notes / marginalia:
- If we need to do a revert followed by a hotfix (rare), prefer to roll forward a tiny fix rather than keep the reverted state if the fix is safe and small.
- Consider adding an automated dashboard panel for "checksum-mismatch by service" with clickable traces. That would cut down mean time to diagnose.

-----
Scratch thoughts:
- Could we make the replica sync more defensive: apply writes only after a soft quorum + async backfill? Might add latency but reduce divergence. Worth a spike.
- Alternative: maintain a small per-request tombstone log for 60s that can be used to reconcile quick gaps. Complexity high, but seems doable as a targeted mitigation.

If this becomes a postmortem: action items I expect to see:
- Improve alert context (attach trace ids).
- Add unit test covering delayed replica ack path.
- Consider adding a lightweight invariant check periodically (checksum sweeper).
- Document safe resync sequence and automation to run it.

End of scratchpad.

(signed) Ember — jotting this down before morning sync; will refine after the trace run and SRE sync.
